top_story.headline: Air Force plans to hire a private airshow announcer, with no competition, to run Dover Air Force Base's 2027 open house
top_story.dek: The sole-source notice names a single individual vendor with no federal contract on record under his name in USAspending.
paragraphs: The Air Force's 436th Contracting Squadron has posted a notice of intent to award a sole-source contract to William David Schultz to serve as air boss, narrator and sound provider for the 2027 First State Airshow and Open House at Dover Air Force Base, Delaware. The notice was posted as a Special Notice. The attached draft performance work statement sets the show for June 12-13, 2027.

The notice's stated reason for skipping competition is that Schultz has more than 200 hours of warbird airshow experience, has run operations with the Thunderbirds, Blue Angels and Snowbirds, and meets specialized FAA and military requirements. No value is stated. USAspending has no federal contract on record under this vendor's name since fiscal 2008.

The draft statement of work goes well beyond directing aircraft. The contractor would produce the show schedule, liaise with the FAA, run the pilot safety briefing, narrate, record promotional announcements for financial sponsors, and supply audio for at least 50,000 spectators along a 5,000-foot crowd line. That includes a control platform of at least 320 square feet, a sound technician on site Friday through Sunday, and generator power at the contractor's expense.

sections.headline: Navy buys two machining centers without competition to speed a White House-backed munitions push
paragraphs: There are 96 new sole-source justifications today, 33 of them posted under other notice types such as Award Notice and Special Notice. None were left out as repeats from earlier editions. Twenty-one are keeping an incumbent's contract running and appear under Extensions, and the Dover airshow notice is the Top Story. A heavy day: five cards and a long second tier are below.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Navy buys two machining centers without competition for rocket-motor production, citing a White House munitions push
meta: Only one company can do it
Department of the Navy, Naval Surface Warfare Center, Corona Division
blocks.text: The justification covers two DN Solutions Mynx 6500 vertical machining centers for the Allegany Ballistics Laboratory in Rocket Center, West Virginia. It says the White House and the Department of War engaged the defense industrial base in July 2025 and set up a Munitions Acceleration Council, and that the plant lacks capacity for the higher rates expected. The Navy says the site already runs a fleet of Mynx 6500s, and that switching models would mean six to eight months of reprogramming. An award notice lists $734,630 to Allegheny Machine Tool Systems Inc. on September 28, although the J&A's own value is redacted.

blocks.title: Trade Representative's office plans to keep a tariff-enforcement support contractor without competition
meta: Executive Office of the President, U.S. Trade Representative (via Interior Business Center)
blocks.text: The Interior Department's contracting arm says it intends to continue buying legal, data-analyst and tariff-expert support for the U.S. Trade Representative from Aalis. Per the notice, the work includes Section 301 trade-enforcement support, China-related analysis, critical-minerals and industrial-sector research, and trade-practice analysis involving Peru lumber. The base period is 2.5 months, and capability statements are due 10:00 a.m. Eastern on October 29, 2026. It was posted as a Special Notice.

blocks.title: Defense Logistics Agency posted its justification after already buying 34.3 million gallons of jet fuel for Jordan

The justification summary cites unusual and compelling urgency from a regional fuel crisis in the Middle East. The notice is a modification under a contract number that dates from fiscal 2025.

blocks.title: Defense Contract Management Agency commits up to $90.5 million to its ServiceNow platform through Carahsoft with no competition

blocks.text: The order covers sustainment, operations, licensing and an expansion of 17 capabilities on the agency's ServiceNow platform, including its UAS Blue List system. Carahsoft is cited as the Defense Department enterprise software agreement holder for ServiceNow at the IL4/IL5 security levels. The justification says only a source with the incumbent's institutional knowledge can avoid delays and duplicated costs.

blocks.title: Navy extends Textron's Aerosonde drone work without competition after the parent authority lapsed in March
meta: Only one company can do it
Department of the Navy, Naval Air Systems Command
blocks.text: The justification covers modifications on three task orders for Aerosonde unmanned aircraft support, transition and mine-countermeasures sensor integration. According to the document, the parent justification for the basic ordering agreement expired in March 2026, so this one is needed to authorize the non-competitive, urgent modifications. Textron is described as the sole designer and OEM. An award notice lists $2,800,695 on September 30.

sections.headline: Housing and Urban Development turns to three firms for $170.8 million of property work without full competition as current contracts end Nov. 1
paragraphs: Twenty-one new justifications mainly keep an existing contractor going: extensions, bridges and ceiling-and-time increases. Four are written up below, and the rest follow in a single list.

blocks.title: Housing and Urban Development picks three firms for $170.8 million of foreclosed-home maintenance without full competition as current contracts end Nov. 1
meta: Alpine Companies Inc., P.K. Management Group Inc., A2Z Field Services
Urgent need, no time to compete
Department of Housing and Urban Development
blocks.text: The class justification covers Field Service Management for foreclosed-property maintenance in eight geographic areas. It says the current base contracts expire November 1, 2026 and the current task-order ordering periods end February 15, 2027. The document says it names these three firms as uniquely capable. It estimates about $126.3 billion in holding costs if newly acquired inventory could not be listed for 30 months.

blocks.title: State Department extends Deloitte's sanctions and AI analytics work for up to two more years without competition
blocks.text: The extension of a blanket purchase agreement call would run one year to September 29, 2027, with two six-month options to September 29, 2028. It supports the Center for Analytics and the sanctions division, whose work the document ties to Russia-Ukraine peace negotiations and Iran sanctions. The state department says Deloitte's cleared staff and knowledge of 30-plus bureaus' data systems make a switch disruptive. The work was originally competed in 2019 under RFQ 19AQMM19Q0144.

blocks.title: National Institutes of Health extends Social & Scientific Systems' epidemiology contract two more years, blaming delays caused by the government-efficiency order
meta: Only one company can do it
blocks.text: The justification raises the ceiling from $112 million to $132 million and extends ordering from June 29, 2026 through June 29, 2028. It says Executive Order 14158, which created the Department of Government Efficiency, caused delays and staffing changes that stalled the recompete. It cites more than three decades of the company's work for the institute.

blocks.title: Air Force extends Peraton's nuclear targeting software work for U.S. Strategic Command without competition
meta: Only one company can do it
blocks.text: The modification extends the period and raises the ceiling on a task order for the NIDS 4 program, which maintains two legacy planning tools and builds their replacements. Per the J&A, users are in U.S. Strategic Command. It says moving to a new contractor mid-transition would cause unacceptable delays. The signed J&A is dated September 23, 2026.

sections.headline: Navy shuts down the F/A-18 Super Hornet production line, with Boeing getting the sole-source job
paragraphs: 544 award notices are new and none repeat earlier editions; 65 were flagged. A $404 million sole-source missile launcher award and a $912,450 neurology contract to a company named Risen Video Production stand out.

blocks.title: Navy gives Boeing $16.7 million without competition to shut down the F/A-18E/F and EA-18G production line
meta: Department of the Navy, Naval Air Systems Command
blocks.text: The delivery order under a basic ordering agreement was signed September 30. A verified document finding says Boeing and its suppliers hold roughly 37,000 items of government-furnished property that only Boeing can account for. The award is phased through 2031, and the document references a 2008 law requiring preservation of special tooling.

blocks.title: Marine Corps gives Kongsberg $404 million for full-rate production of its ship-interdiction missile launchers
meta: Department of the Navy, Marine Corps Systems Command
blocks.text: The sole-source IDIQ, dated September 25, covers full-rate production and sustainment of the Navy/Marine Expeditionary Ship Interdiction System, including launchers, weapon control system and support equipment. The awardee is a Norwegian company.

blocks.title: Veterans Affairs gives a company called Risen Video Production $912,450 for surgical neuromonitoring
blocks.text: The October 14 award is for intraoperative neurophysiologic monitoring. The awardee's name and a Woodland Hills, California address in the award document suggest a video production business, though the notice doesn't say how it will supply neurologists. According to the statement of work, off-site neurologists don't need VA privileging, and the contractor carries its own liability coverage.

meta: Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command
blocks.text: The award is dated July 9, 2026, and the notice was posted October 15. No description beyond the title was posted.

sections.headline: Navy's Marine Raider complex at Camp Lejeune solicitation drew a complaint of unequal access to design drawings
paragraphs: 377 solicitations are new and none repeat earlier ones; 94 were flagged. Heavy news day: three cards, a list, and late findings from documents read today.

blocks.title: Navy's Camp Lejeune Marine Raider facilities solicitation draws questions over classified drawings released then pulled
meta: Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Mid-Atlantic
blocks.text: A bidder question response says certain controlled drawings were first released publicly and later removed, and that access now requires an NDA, which may have given some offerors earlier access. A separate response says the radio-frequency shielded space may not be able to pass full IEEE 299 testing, and that the security plan will be modified to allow U.S. persons rather than only citizens. Funding is $79.5 million on execution with $71.4 million in fiscal 2027.

blocks.title: Immigration and Customs Enforcement extends its AI and data strategy request for information to October 23
blocks.text: The deadline moved from October 16, and answers to questions will come in a later amendment.

items: Customs and Border Protection asks about untrained single-purpose detection canines. (2027K9BPA)
Army sources follow-on Precision Strike Missile Increment 1 production. All 33 files are access-restricted. (PANRSA-26-P-0000-040840)
Defense Information Systems Agency seeks Pentagon security support, following incumbent Kaiva Tech. (832673670)
Coast Guard seeks a live-fire maritime training facility at Camp Lejeune. (70ZL7126R622000001)
Navy seeks a vessel to transfer people and supplies to Ohio-class submarines near Hawaii. (N32205-SS-PM4-27-003)
State Department plans a worldwide fire-alarm replacement contract for about 268 diplomatic facilities. (19AQMM27R0006)

blocks.text: Other flagged notices are mostly construction and ship-repair market research. Routine counts: DLA Aviation, 17; Veterans Affairs offices, about 25.

sections.headline: No new apportionment files were approved in this window
paragraphs: The Office of Management and Budget released no new apportionments or spend plan updates during the October 10–15 period.

footer.coverage_window: October 14-15, 2026 (Pacific time), SAM.gov notices and attached documents.
footer.sources: SAM.gov contract opportunities and their attached documents; OMB apportionment data via openomb.org and apportionment-public.max.gov. USAspending was not run in this PM edition.
footer.known_gaps: No source errors were reported. OMB Apportionments: no new apportionment files were approved in the window. Documents: 4,024 files on 791 notices were identified; 295 are access-restricted on SAM.gov, and 1,708 files are queued and will be read over the next editions, while 84 justification documents were read this run. About 1,800 links to outside portals (DIBBS, NECO, PIEE and others) were not followed.
